findings.section: Wave 9 — W9 — Auth Enforce + Cookie Navigation + Ops Cutover (C2 gate)
findings.criterion: Criterion 2 (One route table, declarative auth, default-deny)
findings.message: The plan specifies shifting browser page navigation to cookie-based authentication in Wave 9, but fails to define the mechanism (e.g. a login/token-exchange endpoint or middleware) by which the browser initially acquires the auth cookie from the ANCHOR_TOKEN. Without this, once token enforcement is activated, legitimate browser users will be locked out unless they manually construct the cookie.

findings.section: Wave 14 — W14 — Parity Gate + Recovery & Replay Tools (C3 gate)
findings.message: Under the 'Journal-first-then-legacy' write ordering (Wave 12), a crash immediately after the journal append but before the legacy store write leaves the database in a journal-ahead state. While the parity gate (Wave 14) tolerates this as 'benign crash residue', the plan does not automate the convergence or replay of these orphaned journal events to the legacy stores on startup, leaving the authoritative read path permanently stale for that mutation.

findings.topic: unhandled abrupt terminal termination on crash
findings.section: Wave 17 — W17 — C4 Live Demo + ConPTY Verdict Application
findings.message: If the ConPTY spike in Wave 3 refutes feasibility, PTYs remain dashboard-owned. The fallback is a graceful pre-restart drain script executed during deploys. However, if the dashboard crashes abruptly or restarts without running the drain script (e.g., manual restart or OS reboot), the active PTY processes will be killed and their states lost, with no automated recovery path specified in the plan.

The global test-command targets specific test files (e.g., test_rearch_2026_07.py) that do not exist at the start of the project. Running this command in early waves (e.g., Wave 1 or 2) will fail pytest with a FileNotFoundError unless empty stub files are explicitly created as part of the Wave 1 setup deliverables.
